newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Megaworld sees 36 pct rise in Q1 net.
newsitem.headline: Megaworld sees 36 pct rise in Q1 net.

text.p: Megaworld Properties and Holdings Inc expects to post a 36 percent rise in first quarter 1997 net profits to 500 million pesos compared with a year ago, Francis Canuto, company treasurer, said on Thursday.
Speaking at an investors' briefing, Canuto also said sales in the first quarter are seen rising 21.4 percent to 2.55 billion pesos from the previous year.
Total assets of the real estate concern posted a year-on-year 84 percent rise to 27 billion pesos during the first quarter, he added.
Company president Andrew Tan reiterated the company's denial that it was facing financial difficulties.

He noted that rumours had included talk the company was cash-strapped, the firm's checks had bounced and that he had fled the country. He called such speculation "irresponsible", adding, "There's definitely no cash-strapped situation here. Our creditors...can attest to our financial state."
Rumours about financial difficulty weakened share prices of Megaworld and its housing developing subsidiary Empire East Land Holdings Inc on Wednesday.
But Tan said the industry was thriving, and that mid- and low-cost housing was seeing a backlog of three million units.
Earlier on Thursday, Tan said Megaworld should see profits rise a minimum of 50 percent in the next five years.
